kurz: How a written investment policy statement, automation, a checklist, a journal and waiting periods ensure that decisions are made before market movements trigger emotions.

bloecke.md:
The previous lessons described typical cognitive biases. This lesson shows how to protect yourself against them with written rules, fixed dates and default settings. Willpower plays no part in this.

The reason is that knowledge about cognitive biases hardly changes behaviour. Even investors who know about their tendency towards [[loss aversion]] still sell in a crash; they can merely name it better. What works are decisions that were made before money and emotions came into play. Formulating a sell rule on a quiet Sunday takes twenty minutes. If the same rule is only drawn up on a day with minus 8%, it costs returns.

## The written investment policy statement

Institutional investors work with an investment policy statement. This document sets out the objective, allocations, limits and responsibilities and is only changed through a regulated procedure. Private investors have no minutes of an investment committee. When they receive investment advice, they at least get a suitability statement (Geeignetheitserklärung) under Section 64(4) WpHG (Securities Trading Act). Anyone who trades through a neobroker without advice gets nothing of the kind and decides afresh each time.

Your own document fits on one page. It contains only sentences that are meant to apply in every market situation, so no market opinion, no price targets and no annual forecast.

bloecke.md: The value of the document lies less in its content than in the time at which it is drawn up. Benjamin Graham recommended a 50/50 split between shares and bonds to the defensive investor. Within a range of 25% to 75% in shares, the investor was allowed to deviate from it according to his own judgement of the price level. Only Graham's simpler variant was mechanical: the allocation is brought back to 50/50 as soon as it has shifted to around 55 to 45. Whether 50/50 is right today is another question; the point here is the design. A range lays down in advance what to do when prices fall, namely to buy more up to the lower limit. Without a range, the same question arises afresh at the most unfavourable moment.
A sell rule can only be formulated sensibly at a time when you do not need it. Anything that is only written down during a crash is a justification after the fact.

## Automation and default settings

The strongest evidence for the effect of default settings does not come from financial research. In 2003 Johnson and Goldstein compared consent rates for organ donation in countries with an opt-in system and countries with an opt-out system. The differences go far beyond ten or twenty percentage points and reach orders of magnitude, with identical effort in filling out forms and practically identical attitudes among the population.

bloecke.titel: Consent to organ donation under opt-in and opt-out
bloecke.unter: The consent rate is decided by the default setting on the form and not by conviction (Johnson/Goldstein, Science 2003).

bloecke.md:
Applied to investing, this means that every decision that has to be made afresh at regular intervals will at some point be made wrongly. It is therefore replaced by a fixed default setting. The savings plan runs on the second banking day and not only “if there is something left at the end of the month”. The annual increase in the monthly contribution follows the same principle. It is decided once and not renegotiated every year. Price alerts are switched off, because every push notification creates an unnecessary evaluation period.

Tax settings, too, can be made once instead of being dealt with anew every year. These include the exemption order (Freistellungsauftrag) for the saver's allowance (Sparer-Pauschbetrag) of €1,000, or €2,000 for joint assessment (Section 20(9) and Section 44a(1) EStG, Income Tax Act), and a sufficient balance in the settlement account for the advance lump sum (Vorabpauschale) to be collected in January (Section 18 InvStG, Investment Tax Act). If this balance is missing, you have to take action in January.

Even a running savings plan that looks good can be based on status quo inertia, for example with the wrong building block, too expensive a provider or a monthly contribution unchanged for five years despite a higher income. Costs are the only return factor whose effect is certain. An ongoing difference of around 1.3 percentage points costs just under a third of the final wealth over 30 years with a lump-sum investment, and about a fifth with a savings plan. That is why the system needs a date on which costs, diversification and the monthly contribution are consciously confirmed or changed.

## The checklist

Atul Gawande transferred the checklist from aviation to the operating theatre. In the WHO study by Haynes and colleagues (New England Journal of Medicine, 2009), mortality in eight hospitals fell from 1.5% to 0.8% and the complication rate from 11% to 7% after a checklist with 19 items was introduced. The surgeons already knew everything on the list beforehand. The list merely ensured that it was also checked under time pressure.

One qualification is that a follow-up study (Urbach et al., NEJM 2014) found no significant improvement after Ontario had made the same checklist mandatory across the board in 2010. A checklist that is only ticked off and not actually applied does not work. The same applies to a portfolio. That is why the following list has at most six items, and each one can be answered with yes or no.

schritte.text: The investment policy statement must contain a sentence that permits this purchase. If there is none, the check ends here.
One sentence on what the market is overlooking, and a figure that supports it. Without a figure there is no position, and a good story does not replace the figure.
Record which event, by what date, would show that the thesis was wrong. Without this sentence, the thesis is only a hope.
The position size follows from the limit in the document and not from your own conviction. Conviction is the worst yardstick for the size of a position.
Work out once what a total loss would mean for your monthly contribution, your timetable and your own sleep.
The decision to do nothing is recorded with a date, like any order. Otherwise the urge to act prevails, because only action produces visible entries.

bloecke.md:
## The cooling-off period

The legislator assumes that people act impulsively and therefore provides for time limits. For insurance contracts, the withdrawal period is 14 days, for life insurance 30 days (Section 8(1) and Section 152(1) VVG, Insurance Contract Act). This construction can be replicated privately where no law offers protection, for example for a securities order that you decide on one evening after watching a video.

A useful house rule is not to buy any security that has been prominent in headlines or feeds in the last 30 days without a seven-day waiting period and a written justification. The same period applies to sales, unless the sale follows a rule laid down in advance. The period occasionally costs a gain. It is nevertheless judged over many cases and not by the individual case. Otherwise you abolish it again after the first missed price jump, even though it is intended precisely for such cases.

bloecke.text: At the stock exchange, two times two is never four, but five minus one.

## The decision journal

A journal records forecasts before memory changes them in hindsight, and so makes them verifiable. It takes five minutes per decision and consists of seven columns.

zeilen: The restructuring of the division is complete, the margin returns to above 12%
Restless, read two days after the quarterly figures
Margin below 9% in 2029, then sell without further review

bloecke.md: The column with the range is the most important one and the hardest to bring yourself to fill in. Forecast intervals are systematically set too narrow. A useful rule of thumb is therefore to double your own 90% interval after writing it down. After twelve months you can count how often the later value was within the range. This gives a figure for your own accuracy and usually a good reason to choose smaller positions.

## Position size as behavioural protection

The expected value of an investment describes the average over many possible paths. An investor, however, experiences only a single path, and along it wealth develops multiplicatively. A setback has to be made up by a gain that is larger in percentage terms, and wealth of zero can no longer grow. That is why ruin is ruled out first and only then is return optimised.

In practice, position size is above all a psychological quantity. It determines whether a position demands attention at night. A 2% position can fall to zero without any rule being broken. A 20% position forces a decision, and does so at the very moment when decisions turn out worst.

bloecke.titel: How a decision runs through the system
bloecke.unter: Impulses pass through the waiting period and the checklist, scheduled dates lead directly to execution, and every path ends in the log.

bloecke.md:
- In January, keep a balance available for the advance lump sum (Section 18 InvStG) and increase the monthly contribution by the pay rise.
- In February, on the review date, compare the allocations with the ranges, check costs and the exemption order (Section 44a(1) EStG) and evaluate the previous year's journal entries.
- Throughout the year, only orders from the calendar or according to the checklist, each one with an entry.
- By 15 December, apply for a loss certificate (Verlustbescheinigung) if you have losses at one bank and gains at another (Section 43a(3) sentences 4 and 5 EStG). Losses on shares can in any case only be offset against gains on shares (Section 20(6) sentence 4 EStG), and partial sales follow the FIFO principle (Section 20(4) sentence 7 EStG). This too belongs in the sell rule and not in the decision of the day.

A pre-mortem reverses the burden of proof. Instead of checking whether a decision is good, you imagine yourself five years in the future and assume as a fact that the venture has failed. Then, in ten minutes, you write down as many reasons for the failure as possible.

The difference from the usual weighing of risks is psychological. Once failure is a given, you look for explanations instead of reassurance. In the process, things regularly come to mind that were missing from the purchase analysis, such as cluster risks, dependence on a single customer or a product that only works when interest rates are low.

The two or three strongest reasons then go into the journal as refutation conditions. In this way the exit is formulated before emotions determine the decision.

mitnehmen: Behaviour changes through fixed structures such as a document, a date, a default setting and a waiting period, and hardly at all through insight.
The investment policy statement fits on one page and contains allocations, ranges, prohibitions and an amendment rule, but no market opinion.
Automatic processes require no perseverance, whereas decisions that are made afresh at regular intervals will at some point turn out wrong.
A checklist with six yes/no questions and doing nothing as a permissible answer only works as long as it is used and not merely ticked off.
Position size determines how much self-control an investment demands, and so serves both risk management and protection against your own behaviour.

begriffe.text: Written document setting out the objective, target allocations, ranges, prohibitions, review dates and an amendment rule. It fixes decisions before market conditions and emotions influence them.

Self-imposed waiting time between an investment idea and the order, usually 24 hours to seven days, combined with a written justification. The model is statutory withdrawal periods such as the one under Section 8 VVG.
Record of every investment decision with the thesis, forecast range, state of mind, refutation condition and review date. It makes your own hit rate measurable instead of leaving it to memory.
Tolerance band around the target allocation, fixed in advance. If it is breached, the portfolio is rebalanced. The question of whether to act is thus replaced by an observable condition.
Exercise in which the failure of a decision is assumed as a fact and the reasons are sought in retrospect. It supplies the refutation conditions for the journal.

Certificate from the bank for losses that have not been offset, so that they can be offset across institutions in the tax return. The application must be made by 15 December (Section 43a(3) sentence 5 EStG).
